html:
SMTO-EXE-0231 — Docker Compose couldn't read this project's settings

GUID: ffc1da36-f4e2-5a98-bd02-23f277fa1726
Slug: docker-compose-config-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • Docker Compose on the Gateway computer couldn't make sense of this project's Compose file, or the service you asked for isn't in it. Nothing was started or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Compare the service name you asked for with the services listed in the project's Compose file, such as compose.yaml, including spelling and capital letters. SMTO stops if the service you named isn't in the project.
  2. Have the project's owner fix any mistakes in the Compose file on the Gateway computer; running docker compose config in the project folder shows the exact problem. SMTO relies on Docker Compose's own check, which fails if the file has errors or missing values.
  3. If the Compose file gets values from a .env file, save that file's full location as a Docker Compose env file parameter in the Parameter Store, and type @ to mention it in your request. SMTO doesn't read a project's .env file on its own, so values from it are missing unless you mention it.
  4. After the fix, ask SMTO to show the project's settings again before you ask it to start, stop or change anything. SMTO only makes changes based on the latest version of the settings it has read.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the project's services, including the one you want.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Compose file, to the person who manages the project. Leave out any passwords or private values when you share the file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • docker compose config for the explicit project failed or returned no services map, a requested service is absent from the resolved configuration, or another read-only Compose command exited with an error.

What this means

  • Compose config execution failed, resolved JSON lacked a services map or the requested service was absent from that resolved configuration. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Compose config execution failed, resolved JSON lacked a services map or the requested service was absent from that resolved configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect bounded config failure, exact files/environment references and requested service membership.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, as the Gateway account, run docker compose config with the same project directory, files, profiles and env files to see the parser error, then fix the file or the requested service name. SMTO sets COMPOSE_DISABLE_ENV_FILE=1, so values from a project .env file load only through a docker_env_file Parameter passed in env_file_refs; read compose_config again to get a fresh revision before any changing Compose operation.
  • Correct the actual configuration or service-selection error and obtain a fresh resolved revision before mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The explicit project resolves valid configuration containing the intended services.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
